cosy-lesson.title: You Must Die First: The Art of Rebirth

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Transformation – a thorough or dramatic change in form or appearance.

p.em: Example: The caterpillar's transformation into a butterfly is a classic symbol of rebirth.

cosy-blockquote.p: Metaphorical – characteristic of or relating to metaphor; figurative.

p.em: Example: When he spoke of "dying first," he was using a metaphorical expression for personal growth.

cosy-blockquote.p: Catalyst – a person or thing that precipitates an event.

p.em: Example: The loss of his job served as a catalyst for him to finally start his own business.

cosy-blockquote.p: Identity – the fact of being who or what a person or thing is.

p.em: Example: Moving to a new country often forces people to re-examine their sense of identity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Renunciation – the formal rejection of something, typically a belief, claim, or course of action.

p.em: Example: Her renunciation of her old lifestyle allowed her to find peace in a simpler way of living.

cosy-blockquote.p: Limitation – a restriction or a point beyond which something does not or may not extend.

p.em: Example: Recognizing your own limitation is the first step toward overcoming it.

cosy-blockquote.p: Resilience ≠ Fragility – the capacity to recover quickly from difficulties ≠ the quality of being easily broken or damaged.

p.em: Example: True resilience is forged by understanding and accepting our own emotional fragility.

cosy-blockquote.p: Paradigm – a typical example or pattern of something; a model.

p.em: Example: The discovery shifted the scientific paradigm and changed how we see the universe.

cosy-blockquote.p: Evolution – the gradual development of something.

p.em: Example: The evolution of his artistic style over twenty years is quite remarkable.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vulnerability ≠ Invulnerability – state of being exposed to the possibility of being attacked or harmed ≠ the state of being impossible to harm or defeat.

p.em: Example: Embracing vulnerability is a far more courageous path than pretending to possess absolute invulnerability.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How does a major life transformation often feel like a loss at the beginning?
★ Philosophers demand that we reflect deeply on life. Is it essential that everyone cultivate inner freedom?

In what ways can a metaphorical death of an old ego lead to better relationships?
★ How comfortable are you with allowing metaphorical to guide your daily decisions?

What has been the most powerful catalyst for change in your professional life?
★ Have you ever felt a deep sense of conflict regarding catalyst in a relationship?

Why is it so painful to let go of an identity that no longer serves us?
★ Can you share a moment from your childhood where identity felt completely natural?

Is the renunciation of material success necessary to find true spiritual fulfillment?
★ How do you personally nurture renunciation when you feel emotionally exhausted?

How does hitting a physical or mental limitation force you to reinvent your approach?
★ Have you ever had to choose between social conformity and personal limitation?

How can we develop the resilience needed to "die" and be "reborn" multiple times in one life?
★ Who in your life best embodies the essence of resilience, and what have they taught you?

What current paradigm in your industry do you think needs to be completely destroyed?
★ In what area of your life do you feel paradigm is most desperately needed right now?

How does the evolution of your values over time make you a different person than you were ten years ago?
★ How has your personal understanding of evolution shifted over the last five years?

Why is vulnerability the key to starting over after a significant failure?
★ If you had to describe your personal experience with vulnerability in one word, what would it be?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, technology will enable us to digitize and share our experience of transformation directly. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you personally adapt if transformation became entirely obsolete in tomorrow's world?

The rapid speed of modern society will eventually make metaphorical an obsolete concept. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you be willing to use technology to artificially boost your capacity for metaphorical?

Future educational systems will prioritize the cultivation of catalyst over traditional academic skills. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you want future generations of your family to remember your relationship with catalyst?

As artificial intelligence advances, machines will exhibit a superior capacity for identity compared to humans. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic school, how would you teach the value of identity to children?

In the coming decades, renunciation will become a highly commercialized luxury commodity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where renunciation is fully managed or monitored by digital algorithms?

The survival of human civilization will depend on our collective ability to practice limitation. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you personally prepare for a future where limitation is increasingly rare?

Future generations will look back at our current understanding of resilience with deep skepticism. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about resilience to people living 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make true paradigm incredibly difficult to maintain in the future. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic utopia that completely guarantees paradigm at the cost of your freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by a person's capacity for evolution rather than wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope evolution will play in your own personal future over the next decade?

A world fully governed by logic will have no space left for the mystery of vulnerability. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a machine could perfectly replicate your experience of vulnerability, would you still value it?

ul.li: Incorrect: I must to die first → Correct: I must die first ((Modal verbs + bare infinitive))
Incorrect: It is a thorough transformation → Correct: It is a thorough transformation ((Spelling: thorough))
Incorrect: I'm not used to take risks → Correct: I'm not used to taking risks ((Used to + -ing))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
Incorrect: It is depend on you → Correct: It depends on you ((Verb vs Adjective))
